title: Chapter 186: New Competition
html:
After collecting his belongings, Chen Ge left the station with the white cat.

This Captain Yan is different from the others.

He glanced back and resolved to keep a low profile for a while. The incident had reminded him that central Jiujiang was not Western Jiujiang. He had avoided trouble before largely because Inspector Lee protected him.

After completing the three-star Trial Mission, there’s no need for me to go unlock other scenarios for now. I should focus on the Third Sick Hall.

In truth, even if a four-star mission were available, Chen Ge would not choose it. Beginning at three stars, the danger multiplied dramatically. Once inside a taxi, he settled the white cat and rooster beside him, then took out the black phone and checked his unread messages.

“Player managed to reach the Mission Location on time and survived until dawn. Trial Mission, Third Sick Hall successful! A new scenario has been unlocked. Player can manipulate the props inside the set freely using the interface available on the phone!

“Trial Mission Completion Rate 60 percent. Player has not achieved more than 90 percent completion rate, so the hidden item for this mission has yet to be unlocked.

“Completing the hidden quest of the scenario will increase the Trial Mission’s completion rate, and when the completion rate is above 90, the hidden item will be unlocked.”

The message stunned Chen Ge. Only sixty percent? What did I miss? Is Men Nan’s original personality hiding something, or does it involve the escaped patients?

Chen Ge looked forward to the hidden reward, and he had noticed a pattern: the higher a Trial Mission’s rating, the more valuable its hidden item and optional objectives. The one-star Ping An Apartments had awarded a missing-person notice imbued with malice, while the two-star Mu Yang High School had yielded a rare ghost—the Pen Spirit.

Could the hidden reward for this three-star mission be the boy?It seemed plausible. Men Nan’s original personality had said that his consciousness had merged with the Third Sick Hall. His relationship with the Third Sick Hall resembles the bond between Director Luo’s daughter and New Century Park. One guards his domain from behind the door; the other watches over hers in the real world.

To discover the Third Sick Hall’s hidden missions, Chen Ge would have to enter the recreated scenario himself. Under the taxi driver’s curious gaze, he gathered his belongings and climbed out. As soon as he entered New Century Park, he noticed visitors casting strange looks his way.

If I’m not mistaken, today isn’t a public holiday, so why are there so many visitors at the park?

The normally quiet amusement park had found new life. Uncomfortable beneath so many stares, Chen Ge hurried toward the Haunted House.

He stopped before reaching it. The queue stretched farther than he could have imagined, and for a moment, he wondered whether he was dreaming.

“Why are there so many visitors?”

“Boss!” Xu Wan stood at the steps of the Haunted House, and she saw Chen Ge as soon as he got near. “You’re finally here!”

Every visitor turned at her shout, and Chen Ge shrank beneath their collective gaze. He squeezed through the crowd and learned from Xu Wan that most of them had come specifically to see him.

The previous night’s broadcast had spread farther than he imagined. Clips had been reposted across major news sites under headlines such as “Fake Livestream Leads to Encounter with Real Murderers.”

Chen Ge now appreciated the brilliance of advertising the Haunted House at the height of the stream’s popularity. He had displayed its address in the largest possible font, forcing anyone who wanted to conceal it to block a quarter of the screen. Rather than ruin the footage, most uploaders had simply left it visible and promoted the attraction for him.

Forums and video platforms across the internet had effectively advertised his Haunted House for free. Many local viewers had decided to visit in person.

His follower count had continued climbing after the broadcast, and comments numbered in the millions. Despite the suspension, he had even broken into the platform’s rankings for popular new hosts.

While Chen Ge reaped the rewards, Qin Guang suffered miserable luck. The platform had invested an unknown fortune in cultivating him, only for repeated technical disasters to end with his stream shut down completely. Rumor claimed the experience frightened Qin Guang into the hospital. Discovering upon waking that Chen Ge’s antics had also gotten his supernatural channel suspended probably made him cough up blood all over again.

With so many visitors, rest was impossible. Fortunately, Chen Ge had slept briefly in the interview room that morning and could still function. After explaining the scenarios’ difficulty levels, he asked Uncle Xu to manage the queue while he and Xu Wan applied their makeup and took their positions.

They had no break all afternoon. Visitors remained in line even as the sun set, forcing the park to delay closing by half an hour. Chen Ge and Xu Wan did not emerge until 6:30 p.m.

With her face white from exhaustion, Xu Wan sighed. “Who would have thought one day, we would need to work overtime at the Haunted House?”

“The future has plenty more surprises waiting. Stay with me, and I promise it will be bright.” Chen Ge smiled at her. Since discovering that he could employ ghosts, his interest in hiring more living staff had diminished considerably. Xu Wan might remain his only living employee for his entire career.

“Boss, there’s something else.” Xu Wan produced a flyer. “A famous traveling Haunted House is coming to Jiujiang. They’ve rented a space in the downtown shopping district, and their grand opening is tomorrow.”

“Competition is healthy. Don’t worry about it.” Chen Ge glanced at the flyer. The attraction, Tian Teng Medical School, blended hospital and school themes in a large mobile Haunted House modeled on Japanese designs.

“I ignored their early promotion too, but when our popularity exploded this morning, they changed the advertisement on their website. Now they claim foreign experts designed their attraction and that it’s unquestionably scarier than every other Haunted House in Jiujiang—a completely different class.” Xu Wan showed him the Tian Teng Medical School website.

The wording did seem deliberately provocative. They never named their target, but Jiujiang’s only other famous Haunted House was Chen Ge’s.

“It appears they want a fight.” Chen Ge kept the flyer. “Don’t worry. When they open tomorrow, I’ll pay them a visit and offer my ‘support.’”
